You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I incorrectly interpreted the question as asking for a comparison between two independent groups (kwox vs. not kwox) rather than evaluating a counterfactual within the same individual. The question asks: "For those who are kwox, would it be less likely to see kwoz if the individual was not kwox?" This requires comparing the probability of kwoz given kwox (65%) against the probability of kwoz given not kwox (35%). Since 35% is indeed less than 65%, the statement "it would be less likely" is true. My error was doubting this straightforward comparison in the self-correction phase and potentially overthinking the causal direction. Next time, I will immediately calculate $P(\text{kwoz} | \neg\text{kwox})$ and compare it directly to $P(\text{kwoz} | \text{kwox})$ without hesitation. Since $35\% < 65\%$, the correct answer is "Yes".
